prize_parts.citation: For the development of palladium-catalysed carbon-nitrogen cross-coupling, a general catalytic route to aryl amines

statement.case_for: My preferred configuration is unchanged: B032 as a single part, credited to Hartwig and Buchwald. After round 1 no position has a majority, and the B063 supporters have not yet answered the maturity and attribution problems. I therefore keep to the criteria I can test. The discovery is new chemistry: amido-palladium intermediates are prone to beta-hydride elimination and reductive elimination to C-N is slow, so the catalytic version needed ligand design and not just the earlier C-C coupling logic. It is general, ligand-controlled and used daily at industrial scale for aryl amines in drugs, agrochemicals and materials. Attribution is a clean pair, with independent mid-1990s catalytic work by both and then successive ligand generations from each. It has been reproduced for over 25 years. I do not claim it is the most fashionable candidate. I claim it carries the least risk on originality, credit and maturity at once.
statement.case_against: The strongest objection remains the 2010 cross-coupling prize (Heck, Negishi, Suzuki), which some members will treat as already covering Pd-catalysed bond formation. The Kosugi and Migita tin-amide precedent has to be handled in the citation wording or it will be raised after the announcement. The candidate has support from only one member as a first choice and appears in few opening ballots, so a majority is unlikely unless the committee decides that a mature, well-attributed method should outweigh breadth of support. Finally, I am the only synthetic organic chemist on the committee and my field bias toward this method is real.

responses.point: Linke, as chair, moved B063 to first place because the credit divides into a concept strand (Crews, Deshaies) and a mechanism strand (Handa on cereblon), and he asked whether the lack of an approved degrader is disqualifying now.
responses.response: That division of credit is the first argument that makes a three-name B063 citation look defensible to me, and I count it as progress. It does not remove my reservation. The concept strand and the mechanism strand were developed separately, and a citation joining them rests on a later unifying idea, induced proximity, more than on one discovery. On the chair's question about approval, I would not call the absence of a degrader drug disqualifying in principle. I do think that a modality which has not yet delivered an approved drug is not a stronger case than a method with 25 years of use. I continue to rank B063 as my first alternative, and an approval would move it up for me. I also note that Linke's own reasoning for dropping B031, entangled credit and doubtful status as chemistry, is why I keep it only as a second alternative.

responses.point: Aili prefers B063 for the PROTAC and cereblon-glue citation, and would give the third place to Handa over Ciulli, accepting that no degrader is approved and that two historically separate achievements are being merged.
responses.response: I follow the Handa-over-Ciulli logic if the citation must include the cereblon mechanism. That choice, however, leaves out the person who made PROTACs drug-like through VHL ligand design, and Aili's own case against lists this as a weakness. A citation worded from PROTACs to molecular glues has to explain why Ciulli and Ito stand outside it, and I cannot yet see a wording that does so without sounding arbitrary. Aili is right that breadth of opening support is not merit, and by the same standard B063 should be judged on maturity and credit, where I find it weaker than B032.

responses.point: Zou prefers molecular-sieve catalysts (B051) as a fully mature field of large industrial reach, and asks whether it is distinct enough from the 2025 framework-materials prize, while admitting that the choice among Corma, Davis, Zones, Yu and Tsapatsis is subjective.
responses.response: We agree that maturity should carry weight, and that a field with decades of independent confirmation is safer than a modality still being proven. We differ on credit. The Corma, Davis, Zones triple is chosen from five claimants and Zou says the choice is partly subjective, whereas the C-N coupling pair is not in doubt. I would add that B051 and B032 face the same kind of objection, overlap with a recent or earlier prize. I think zeolites are the further from the 2025 prize, but I find the attribution burden decisive. I do not consider proximity to the field a reason for Zou to recuse, and I would say the same of my own position.

responses.point: Chabes weighs the breadth of support for B063 (eight of eight members ranked it) more than any single member's enthusiasm, and asks what clinical milestones would be sufficient.
responses.response: I accept that eight of eight ranking is a real signal that every member finds the idea serious. I do not accept it as a decision rule, because a candidate everyone places fourth to sixth is different from one that a member regards as the best. On milestones, I would want at least one approved degrader or pivotal-trial success, and a settled answer on whether the citation covers PROTACs, glues or both. Chabes also raised the Kosugi and Migita question for B032 in round 1. I still think a citation worded around the catalytic, general amination handles it without a third name, and I would add a sentence on the precursors to the citation background and not to the prize text.

uncertainties: Whether a majority will treat C-N coupling as separate from the 2010 cross-coupling prize or as its extension.
Whether the citation should carry any acknowledgment of the Kosugi and Migita tin-amide precedent, and where.
Whether the committee will accept a mature method with narrow first-choice support over a broadly ranked but unproven modality such as B063.

A correction to my round-1 note: photoredox catalysis (B009), which I ranked second, is on the shortlist. Its credit is spread over seven names and I could not pick a clean three, so I leave it out of my configuration. I could be persuaded to add it as a second part only if a one-person part were acceptable, which I doubt, since the three-person limit leaves one place beside Hartwig and Buchwald.
statement.conflict_note: No change. I have no collaboration, mentorship or institutional tie to Buchwald, Hartwig, Kosugi or any other shortlisted candidate. My field is synthetic organic methodology, so I carry a field bias toward B032, and I ask colleagues to weigh my preference with that in mind. I do not see a need for recusal. My Lund affiliation is shared with Linke and Sparr, who are committee members and not candidates.
